description: Vocabulary related to news reporting, life stories, and past time expressions.

words.example: Welcome. I’m Ron Boyd, and with me tonight is reporter Veronica Mendez.
Tonight, we hear first news stories from our reporters around the globe.
Brennan was on a camping trip with his Boy Scout troop and got lost in the mountains.
His family created a website asking for volunteers to help find him.
Ollie Hicks left New York to cross the Atlantic in a red rowboat.
He had hoped to break the record of 62 days for the slowest crossing.
Katharine Close has just won the Scripps National Spelling Bee.
The man was following the instructions from his car’s navigation system.
His trip ended when he crashed into a pile of sand.
Last year, she came in seventh place as a contestant in the spelling bee.
A burglar stole $100 in cash and a computer from the house.
Because there was no sign of a break-in, the police are sure the dog opened the door.
Frieda, an octopus at the Munich Zoo, has learned how to open jars of seafood snacks.
All we did was open some jars where she could see us, says a zoo attendant.
Mary Brown was very angry when her ex-husband remarried.
When the couple returned two weeks later, the phone bill was $8,000.
An angry emu chased a 10-year-old girl up a tree in her backyard.
Australian firefighters rescued a girl after she was chased by an emu.
We’re looking at that section of the paper with all the funny, odd news stories.
This is at the top of a story in the newspaper.
You can find small ads in the classifieds section of a newspaper.
You vote for your favorite leader in an election.
You read a magazine weekly or monthly for news and entertainment.
While they were on their honeymoon, a former wife went to their apartment.
Take part in this competition and you may win a prize!
A trophy is a kind of prize given to the winner of a contest.
You can find the latest local news in this section of the paper.
Most people prefer a story with a happy ending.
